text:
Washington and Ottawa both arrive off wins three days ago. The Capitals beat Florida 4-3, with Jack St. Ivany scoring his first NHL goal, and are 3-2-0 in their last five while missing Vincent Desharnais. The Senators beat Utah 4-2 and are 3-1-1 in their last five, but they are without William Eklund (ankle) until early January at the earliest. Tim Stützle has moved onto the line beside Cozens and Zetterlund, and Ridly Greig, cleared by ESPN, could return.

Our numbers see little between them. At five on five, WSH has 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and OTT 52%, and we project 3.22 goals for the Senators against 3.08 for the Capitals. The matchup to watch is Ottawa's power play, which creates 0.76 expected goals a game, against a Washington penalty kill that allows 0.87. The Senators also take 4.7 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays.

In net, projected starters Logan Thompson and Linus Ullmark have gone opposite ways. Ullmark has saved 8.2 goals above expected this season but was at -13.3 last year, while Thompson is at +1.9 after a +28.2 season.

Stützle is the best bet to produce, with a 77% chance at a point and 36% to score. Alex Tuch, who scored in Washington's last game, is at 38% to score. Ryan Leonard plays his 100th NHL game.
